title: Catalog entry affordance lab notes and copy scenarios
content:
Purpose / TL;DR:
Quick experimental notes from a short design lab focused on making the model-catalog -> endpoint-create flow feel fast and safe for engineers. Emphasis: single-click discoverability for compatible model versions, low-friction temporary pins, and clear fallback messaging when a selected model version is incompatible with chosen instance types or quantization settings. This doc captures wireframe annotations, alternate microcopy options we tested, unresolved edge cases, and proposed backlog tickets.

Audience:
- PM/designers: prioritize UX decisions for next sprint
- Eng: feasibility notes for backend hooks (version metadata, compatibility checks)
- Solutions/SRE: rollout/fallback expectations

Context:
We ran a 90-minute lab with 4 participants (internal eng+pm reps) to iterate on two prototype screens: (A) catalog detail card expanded overlay and (B) quick-endpoint modal (inline, 3 step). Goal: reduce time from catalog → working endpoint from ~3 mins to <60s for a common happy path.

Wireframe notes (overlay mode):
- Trigger: clicking model card title opens an overlay rather than full nav change. Rationale: keeps catalog context, faster dismissal.
- Top row: name / tags / last-indexed (small). Under that, a compact dropdown list of compatible model versions; each version row shows: version id, short latency estimate (p50 / p95) for the selected region, and a small badge for compatibility issues (# if any).
- Select a version: choose button becomes primary CTA "Create endpoint with vX" (default) and secondary CTA "Run sample" (opens ephemeral playground).
- Compatibility tooltip: hover on badge reveals exact mismatch (e.g., "Requires cuDNN 9 kernels — not supported on Dedicated-small"). We propose a copy pattern: start with problem then next actionable step.
- Version search: small fuzzy-search box to find versions by commit/tag/notes. Helpful when there are 20+ variants.

Wireframe notes (quick-endpoint modal — inline 3-step):
Step 1 — Basic: endpoint name (prefilled: model-name-YYYYMMDD), region picker, capacity tier (hosted/dedicated/private).
Step 2 — Variant config: chosen version (dropdown from overlay), quantization preset (auto suggestion), batch size recommendation.
Step 3 — Review & create: stability estimate, expected cost per 1k tokens, and two toggles: "Enable auto-fallback to earlier compatible version" and "Enable request-level KV cache sharing".

Copy candidates (button + microcopy variations):
- Primary CTAs tried:
  1) "Create endpoint" (neutral)
  2) "Deploy as endpoint" (slightly more formal)
  3) "Start serving" (action-focused)
  4) "Create endpoint with vX" (explicit variant) — currently preferred in lab since it reduces follow-up uncertainty.

- Variant helper text (below version dropdown):
  - Option A: "Selected variant: v7 · Optimized for latency (use for chat)."
  - Option B: "v7 — latency-focused. Switch to v7-ff for lower cost."
  - Option C (more verbose): "v7 (recommended) — best latency/cost for short-turn conversational workloads."

- Compatibility error phrasing: we iterated on tone to avoid alarmism while being specific. Candidates:
  - "This version requires hardware features not available in the chosen tier. Select a different tier or choose v6 (compatible)."
  - "Version v7 uses kernels unavailable on Dedicated-S. Switch tier or pick v6."
  - Preferred shorter assistant-tone: "v7 can't run on Dedicated‑S. Pick a different tier or choose v6 (one click to switch)."

- Fallback toggle copy:
  - Label: "Auto-fallback to compatible version"
  - Description candidate 1: "If the selected version is unavailable, automatically serve using the most recent compatible variant."
  - Description candidate 2 (short): "Automatically fall back to a compatible variant to avoid failures."

Design heuristics & rationale:
- Make the selected version visible everywhere in the creation flow (prevents accidental mismatch between catalog selection and endpoint config).
- Explicit actions > implicit defaults. Users should opt-in to background magic (e.g., aggressive quantization or fallbacks).
- Keep modals small and scannable: limit to two primary CTAs per step.
- Use inline compatibility checks (non-blocking) with gentle red/orange badges rather than full-blocking errors unless the conflict is unrecoverable.

Edge cases / unresolved items:
1) If user pins a private model version that is later deleted/removed, what should happen for existing endpoints? (propose: endpoints keep immutable copy of pinned model metadata and fallback to the last known compatible variant; ticket needed to design archive flow).
2) Version tags vs. commit SHAs — how visible should the full SHA be? Tradeoff between traceability and UI noise. Suggestion: show short 7-char SHA on hover; show friendly tag by default.
3) Bulk-create endpoints from multiple selected models — skip for now (out of scope).
4) When enabling "auto-fallback", we need a clear audit trail/alerting: user must be able to see which requests used fallback (console + logs).

Backlog proposals (short tickets to create):
- PRD: CL-311 Endpoint creation UX — make selected variant persistent across steps (owner: Maya)
- ENG: API-527 Add version compatibility metadata to model catalog endpoints (owner: Diego)
- SRE: SRE-129 Design fallback metrics to surface in Console (requests using fallback, fallback rate)
- DOCS: DOC-88 Microcopy styleguide for error/compatibility messaging (owner: Priya)

Metrics to validate success:
- Time to first working endpoint (median) — target: reduce from 180s -> 60s for standard path
- Rate of endpoint-creation failures due to version/tier mismatch — target: <1%
- Clicks from catalog to endpoint create — target: 2 click happy path (card -> overlay -> create)

Prototype links and where we tested:
- Figma: (prototype frame) https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/catalog-quick-lab
- Recorded lab session (internal): https://drive.mock/redwood/sessions/lab-2025-01-07.mp4

Next steps (this sprint):
- Lock microcopy for compatibility badge + primary CTA (Maya/Design) — deliver final text for engineering by Jan 21
- Small backend spike for compatibility metadata + quick response surface (Diego) — estimated 3 dev days
- Add telemetry hooks for fallback events (SRE + Eng) — spike and acceptance criteria in SRE-129
- Run an A/B with 200 users: "explicit version in CTA" vs "generic Create endpoint" to measure drop-off (PM + analytics)

Notes to reviewers:
- Please flag any security or policy implications for "auto-fallback" (particularly for Private deployments).
- If copy feels too technical for product engineers, propose simpler phrasing in comments.

Unfinished microscopy snippets (for follow-up experiments):
- "Run sample with this variant" vs "Try sample" — which suggests more isolation?
- "Pin version for this endpoint" vs "Lock version" — tone tradeoffs: pin = friendly, lock = adminy.

End of doc.

Revision history:
- 2025-01-07 created (Maya) — initial notes from lab
- 2025-01-10 added copy variants and edge case list (Priya)
- 2025-01-15 added backlog ticket mapping and prototype links (Diego)
